title: Emissions, climate and policy: the system together
summary: Put all the boxes back together. Follow emissions into Hector, see how GCAM implements carbon prices and caps, and trace five feedback loops that only an integrated model can show.
outcomes: You can explain how GCAM's emissions reach Hector and become warming
You can describe a carbon price, an emissions cap and a climate target in GCAM
You can trace at least five cross-component feedback loops
You can contrast GCAM's market equilibrium with an optimisation model
narration_en: This module puts all the boxes back together. Emissions come from burning fuels, from land use change and from other gases such as methane and nitrous oxide. In every period GCAM passes them to Hector, a simple climate model, which turns them into concentrations, radiative forcing and global temperature. Policies close the loop. A carbon price is the simplest: you choose the price path and the model finds the emissions. An emissions cap works the other way round: you choose the emissions and the model finds the price that achieves them, and a climate target goes one step further and finds the price path that meets a temperature or forcing goal. Because everything is linked, a single policy ripples through the system. A carbon price raises bioenergy demand, which raises land prices and food prices. It also pays landowners for carbon, which grows forests, and it raises the electricity price, which shifts transport and buildings. In this module you will run a tiny integrated model with a price and a cap, and see that both doors open onto the same room.
narration_ar: تعيد هذه الوحدة تجميع كل الصناديق معًا. تأتي الانبعاثات من حرق الوقود، ومن تغيّر استخدام الأرض، ومن غازات أخرى مثل الميثان وأكسيد النيتروز. وفي كل فترة يمررها نموذج GCAM إلى نموذج هيكتور المناخي البسيط، الذي يحولها إلى تركيزات وتأثير إشعاعي ودرجة حرارة عالمية. وتُغلق السياسات الحلقة. أبسطها سعر الكربون: تختار مسار السعر ويجد النموذج الانبعاثات. أما سقف الانبعاثات فيعمل بالعكس: تختار الانبعاثات ويجد النموذج السعر الذي يحققها، ويذهب الهدف المناخي خطوة أبعد فيجد مسار السعر الذي يحقق هدفًا لدرجة الحرارة أو للتأثير الإشعاعي. ولأن كل شيء مترابط، تنتشر سياسة واحدة في النظام كله. فسعر الكربون يرفع الطلب على الطاقة الحيوية، مما يرفع أسعار الأرض والغذاء. ويدفع أيضًا لملاك الأراضي مقابل الكربون، فتنمو الغابات، ويرفع سعر الكهرباء، فيتغير النقل والمباني. في هذه الوحدة ستشغّل نموذجًا متكاملًا صغيرًا بسعر وبسقف، وترى أن البابين يفتحان على الغرفة نفسها.

diagram.title: The whole system and its feedbacks
diagram.caption: Five loops to trace: bioenergy–food, carbon–forest, electricity–transport, water–cooling, and emissions–climate–policy.

nodes.label: Economy
nodes.detail: Population and GDP drive every demand (Go 2.1). In open-GDP mode energy feeds back to GDP.

nodes.label: Markets and solver
nodes.detail: Broyden's method clears a few hundred markets each period (Go 2.2).

nodes.label: Energy
nodes.detail: Resources, conversion and end uses (Go 2.4, 2.5). Shares by nested logit (Go 2.3).

nodes.label: Land and food
nodes.detail: Crops, pasture, forest and energy crops share land by profit (Go 2.6).

nodes.label: Water
nodes.detail: Basin prices from renewable, groundwater and desalination tiers (Go 2.7).

nodes.label: Emissions
nodes.detail: CO₂ from fuels × carbon coefficients, land-use change CO₂, and non-CO₂ gases with MAC curves (emissions.html).

nodes.label: Hector
nodes.detail: Each period GCAM passes emissions to Hector v3.2, which computes concentrations, forcing and global temperature (hector.html).

nodes.label: Policy
nodes.detail: fixedTax price paths, emissions constraints solved for a price, or climate targets via target-finder mode (policies.html).

nodes.label: Reference vs policy
nodes.detail: Results are read as policy run minus reference run; never as forecasts.

tour.text: Drivers set demands; the solver finds prices that clear every market in the period.
Loop 1, bioenergy–food: energy demand for biomass raises land and food prices.
Loop 2, carbon–forest: a carbon price on land pays for stored carbon and expands forests.
Loop 3, water–cooling: scarce basins raise water prices and shift power-plant cooling.
Loop 4, electricity–transport: carbon prices change electricity costs, shifting EVs and heat pumps.
All emissions go to Hector, which returns concentrations, forcing and temperature.
Loop 5, climate target: the price path is adjusted until the target is met. Read results as policy minus reference.

sections.heading: Emissions
sections.html:
CO₂ = fuel use × carbon coefficients (consistent with CDIAC), plus cement process CO₂, fugitive CO₂ and land-use change CO₂. Non-CO₂ greenhouse gases (CH₄, N₂O, F-gases) use marginal abatement cost (MAC) curves that read the carbon price:

Et = At · Ft0 · (1 − MAC(pricet))

The MAC curves were updated in v8.9. Outputs: CO₂ in MtC/yr, non-CO₂ in Tg/yr; net CO₂ = CO₂ emissions by region + LUC emissions (emissions.html, outputs_emissions.html).

sections.heading: Climate: Hector inside GCAM
sections.html:
Each period GCAM passes its emissions to Hector v3.2, which computes concentrations, radiative forcing and temperature. The coupling is one-way via emissions: climate impacts on yields or runoff are not automatic in core GCAM (hector.html). The kit's toy climate model (impulse-response carbon cycle + two-layer energy balance; not Hector) gives: flat 40 Gt/yr → 637 ppm and 2.53 °C in 2100; net zero by 2050 → 443 ppm and 1.52 °C.

F = 5.35 · ln(C / C0) W/m²

sections.heading: Policy: price, cap, target
sections.html:
A carbon price (fixedTax) is set by you; a constraint caps emissions and GCAM solves for the price; a climate target (target-finder mode, find-path=1) searches for the least-cost price path to a forcing, temperature or concentration goal and "substantially increases run time". Carbon prices are in 1990$ per tonne of carbon (policies.html, user-guide.html).

In the kit's toy system, a cap of −50% by 2050 is met by a price starting at $2.5/t in 2025 growing 5% a year: a price and a cap are two doors to the same room.

sections.heading: Five feedback loops
sections.html:
1. Bioenergy → land → food: biomass demand raises energy-crop profit, shifting cropland and raising food prices.
  2. Carbon price → land carbon → forests: the land carbon subsidy expands forest; crops intensify.
  3. Water scarcity → cooling: rising basin prices move power from once-through to recirculating or dry cooling.
  4. Electricity price → transport and buildings: cheaper clean power pulls EVs and heat pumps in, raising electricity demand.
  5. Emissions → Hector → target: in target-finder mode the price path adjusts until the climate goal is met.

sections.heading: Equilibrium versus optimisation
sections.html: GCAM finds market equilibria period by period with no foresight. Optimisation models such as MESSAGEix choose the least-cost system over the whole century with perfect foresight; the shadow price of an emissions cap plays the role of the carbon price. In the week 11 linear program (coal, gas, solar; 100 TWh) a 40 Mt cap gives coal 22.2, gas 50, solar 27.8 TWh at a shadow price of about $22 per tonne. Both paradigms answer "what if", not "what will be".

callouts.title: In GCAM
callouts.html: Queries: CO2 emissions by region, global mean temperature, CO2 prices. Policy example files ship in input/policy; the course carbon price file is carbon_price_global.xml and the net-zero setup is in lab10_netzero_config_snippet.xml (policies_examples.html).

callouts.title: Units of the carbon price
callouts.html: GCAM reports carbon prices in 1990$ per tonne of carbon. Multiply by 12/44 to get $/tC from $/tCO₂, or by 44/12 the other way, and convert the dollar year before comparing with studies.

callouts.title: A useful mental model
callouts.html: Push on one box of a mobile hanging from the ceiling and every other box moves. A single carbon price moves energy, land, water and emissions together; that movement is what an integrated model is for.

explorer.intro: Set a starting carbon price and its growth rate; watch the price path and the cut it buys on a simple cost curve.

takeaways: Emissions from fuels, land and non-CO₂ gases go to Hector each period
A carbon price fixes the price; a cap fixes emissions and GCAM finds the price
Climate targets search for a price path and take much longer to run
One policy moves energy, land, water and emissions together through feedback loops
Read every result as policy minus reference, not as a forecast

quiz.q: Under an emissions constraint in GCAM, the carbon price is…
options: solved by the model to meet the cap
quiz.explain: The cap is a market; its solved price is the carbon price.

quiz.q: Climate impacts on crop yields in core GCAM are…
options: not automatic; they must be imposed as inputs
quiz.explain: The coupling is one-way via emissions (hector.html).

quiz.q: Which loop links bioenergy to food prices?
options: Energy demand for biomass → land competition → crop prices
quiz.explain: Energy crops compete with food crops in the cropland nest.

quiz.q: The key difference between GCAM and MESSAGEix is that GCAM…
options: solves period by period without foresight
